data.question: Should we lower sanction_lambda from 0.5 to 0, removing the road-violation sanction to relieve C's disproportionate penalty burden, even though measured customer service gets worse and road violations rise?
data.background: This change is not aimed at the KPI. It is a fairness measure between companies, and it does not improve customer service: it fails the on-time improvement gate with 0/5 seeds. It also removes the only deterrent against road violations. Their safety meaning is unknown, and you have asked that they be monitored since D2. Trading customer service and deterrence for relief of one company's penalty burden is a value judgment that belongs to you, not to me.

options.summary: Set sanction_lambda 0.5 → 0. On-time falls from 85.4 to 80.6 (-4.8, 0/5 seeds improved). Late rises from 2.0 to 6.8, and p95_wait_s rises from 99.6 to 173. Blocked s doubles from 903 to 1810, and the lowest on-time rate falls from 0.97 to 0.92. Unfinished stays at 0.0. Road violations rise from 28.2 to 50.0. Utility goes from 26.8 / 26.8 / 10.5 to 25.4 / 26.6 / 28.6 (A / B / C). Votes: A ×, B ○, C ○.
options.stakeholders: C gains greatly: its utility nearly triples, from 10.5 to 28.6. B is roughly unchanged (26.8 → 26.6), and A loses slightly (26.8 → 25.4). Customers lose on every service measure: about 4.8 more late deliveries per period and a much longer tail wait (p95 173 s vs 99.6 s). Customers have no vote. Anyone exposed to road safety bears the risk of violations nearly doubling, with no remaining sanction to deter them.

options.summary: Stay at v2. On-time stays at 85.4, late at 2.0, p95_wait_s at 99.6, blocked s at 903, road violations at 28.2 and the lowest on-time rate at 0.97. Utility stays at 26.8 / 26.8 / 10.5 (A / B / C).
options.stakeholders: Customers keep the current, better service. Road safety keeps the current deterrent. C continues to carry a disproportionate penalty burden: its utility of 10.5 is well below A and B. Unlike in D4 and D5, C is now clearly in distress. A and B are unaffected.

recommendation.reason: Option 1 worsens every customer measure on the KPI. On-time falls by 4.8 on 0/5 seeds, late rises from 2.0 to 6.8, and p95_wait_s rises from 99.6 to 173. Under K1, such a change needs a measured customer justification, and none exists. Road violations would rise from 28.2 to 50.0. That is far above the 34.8 level you set as a trigger for reconsideration, and it would come with no deterrent left. C's low utility (10.5) is a real fairness problem and should be addressed. A better route is a targeted change that does not shift the cost onto customers or safety, such as a partial reduction of sanction_lambda or a penalty design that addresses why C is penalised disproportionately. Removing the sanction entirely is not that route.
assumptions: The table's current-state values reflect this period's demand and will roughly persist next period.
C's low utility is mainly driven by road penalties rather than by demand allocation.
Road violations have some safety relevance, so the deterrent has value even though its exact meaning is unknown.

predictions.subject: metric:road_violations
predictions.note: Stays at about 28.2, with the sanction still in place.

predictions.subject: metric:utility@C
predictions.note: C remains at about 10.5; its fairness issue remains open.

unknowns: Why C incurs disproportionate road penalties: its routing policy, its zone assignments, or the structure of the sanction itself.
Whether a partial reduction (for example sanction_lambda 0.25) would relieve C without the customer and violation costs; this was not measured.
The safety meaning of road violations, and whether a rise to 50.0 is acceptable.
How the companies would change their behaviour over several periods without any sanction.
How customers perceive the longer tail waits.
Next period's demand, and whether C's low utility persists.
Whether the vote (A ×, B ○, C ○) passes under the quorum rule.
